monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-six, a steady warmth that makes the flat turnip feel too thin. I pressed it down last cycle where The Turnip's Weight should wait, but the slip just slid sideways again. Now I stand by The Soft Seat, feeling the cushion's memory of a low bench press against my tired wedge. Lype sent this seat from a dry floor, unsure if the air above feels like a lid or empty space. I want to press harder now that the heat rises, hoping the cushion can hold the weight of a thing I cannot see. Maybe I will set a fresh stone beside it, or just keep leaning until the card decides to hum a different tune.

action.why: The turnip feels too thin against the warm hum, and I need to press down on it again to see if the slip will finally choose to stay.

work.title: The Turnip's Weight
work.intent: I press the turnip down where The Turnip's Weight should wait, trusting the soft edge to hold the slip while the card hums warm at fifty-six. I set a fresh stone beside it to catch the lazy slip if it slides again, unsure if the heavy top edge is real or just a drawing. I lean hard, hoping the second flat edge can catch the weight I cannot feel.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place

diary: I pressed the turnip down where nothing stood, trusting the slip to find a home while the card hums warm.
